Rashi on Bava Metzia 16b:10:1.hebrew: כל מעשה ב"ד - קס"ד שטר שכתב בו הנפק שנתקיים בב"ד, אלמא כיון דליכא למיחש לשמא לא לוה — שהרי אין מקיימין את השטר אלא בפני בעל דין, כדאמרי' בהגוזל (ב"ק דף קיב:) — לפרעון לא חיישינן:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 16b:10:1.english: Any court enactment - It was initially assumed [that this refers to] a document in which a henpek [court authentication] was written, that was authenticated in court. Thus, since there is no reason to be concerned that perhaps he did not borrow — for we only authenticate a document in the presence of the litigant, as we say in [the chapter] HaGozel (Bava Kamma 112b) — we are not concerned about repayment.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 16b:10:2.hebrew: בשטרי חלטאתא - שטר שכתבו בי"ד למוציא שטר על חבירו, וחייבוהו לשלם ולא שילם, וירדו לנכסיו ושמו לבעל חוב אחד מהם, ונתנו לו שטר שעל פי בי"ד באה לו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 16b:10:2.english: With regard to bills of foreclosure - A document that the court wrote for one who produces a [promissory] note against his fellow, and [the court] obligated him to pay, and he did not pay, so they entered upon his property and appraised one of them for the creditor, and gave him a document [stating] that it came to him by order of the court.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 16b:10:3.hebrew: אדרכתא - שלא מצאו לו עכשיו נכסים, וכתבו לו שירדוף לחזור על נכסיו, ואם ימצא יגבה. אדרכתא — לשון רודף ומשיג, כמו "פרסה בחלא ולא אדרכיה" (כתובות דף ס:), ולשון המקרא: "כתרו את בנימין הרדיפוהו מנוחה הדריכוהו" (שופטים כ׳:מ״ג):
Rashi on Bava Metzia 16b:10:3.english: Adrakhta [a bill of authorization] - Where they [the court] did not find property belonging to him [the debtor] right now, and they wrote for him [the creditor] that he may pursue and search for his property, and if he finds [any], he may collect [from it]. Adrakhta is an expression of pursuing and overtaking, as in "[he pursued him] a parasang in the sand, and he did not overtake him" (Ketubot 60b), and the language of Scripture: "They surrounded Benjamin, pursued them, [at] Menuchah they overtook them" (Judges 20:43).

Rashi on Bava Metzia 16b:11:1.hebrew: שומא - ששמו ב"ד לבעל חוב קרקע הלוה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 16b:11:1.english: Appraisal - [Where] the court appraised the borrower's land for the creditor.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 16b:11:2.english: [It] is returned - If [the debtor] pays [the creditor] money within a year.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 16b:12:1.hebrew: אפסיד אנפשיה - אם פרע ולא קרע השטר, ואם דחהו לומר אבד, היה לו לומר: כתוב לי שטר מיד שאתה חוזר ומוכרה לי:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 16b:12:1.english: He caused the loss to himself - If he repaid [the debt] and did not tear up the document; and if [the creditor] put him off by saying, "[It] was lost," he should have said [to him], "Write a document for me immediately [stating] that you are selling it back to me."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 16b:13:1.hebrew: דמדינא ארעא לא בעי למיהדר - טעם נותן לדבריו, שראוי לכתוב שטר מכירה עליה, שקנויה לו לחלוטין ומדינא לא בעי למיהדר בפדיון אם לא מדעתו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 16b:13:1.english: That by law the land need not be returned - [He] gives a reason for his words, that it is fitting to write a bill of sale for it, because it is acquired by him completely and by law [it] need not be returned upon redemption unless [it is] with his consent.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 16b:13:2.hebrew: מרישא דקא זבין - כלומר, אין זה פדיון אלא תחילת קניין כאילו שלו היתה. לפיכך, הכותב שטר מכירה עליה אינו טועה, והיה לו לזה לתבוע שטר מכירה, הואיל ודחהו מלהחזיר לו שטר של ב"ד:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 16b:13:2.english: [It is] anew that he is purchasing [it] - That is to say, this is not a redemption, but rather the start of an acquisition as though [the land] had been his [the creditor's]. Therefore, one who writes a bill of sale for it is not mistaken, and this one [the debtor] should have demanded a bill of sale, since [the creditor] put him off from returning the court document to him.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 16b:14:1.hebrew: אי נמי אפשיטי דספרא זייר ליה - שעל הלוה ליתן שכר הסופר, ופעמים שאין לו מעות ללוה בשעת הלואה, והמלוה נותן לו שכר לכתיבת השטר, וכשפרעו מעכב השטר בידו עד שיפרע השכר:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 16b:14:1.english: Alternatively, he holds it back for the scribe's fee - For it is [incumbent] upon the borrower to pay the scribe's fee, and sometimes the borrower does not have money at the time of the loan, so the lender pays [the scribe] the fee for writing the note; and when [the borrower] repays him, [the lender] retains the note in his possession until [the borrower] pays the fee.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 16b:14:2.hebrew: זייר - לשון עוצר, כמו מעצרתא זיירא (ע"ז דף ס.), ובלשון המקרא: ויזר את הגזה (שופטים ו׳:ל״ח):
Rashi on Bava Metzia 16b:14:2.english: He held [it] back [zayeir] - [This is] an expression of withholding [or pressing], like "a tightened press [ma'atzarta zaira]" (Avodah Zarah 60a), and in the language of Scripture: "and he wrung out [vayazar] the fleece" (Judges 6:38).

Rashi on Bava Metzia 16b:17:1.hebrew: כל מעשה ב"ד - והאי נמי מעשה ב"ד הוא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 16b:17:1.english: Any court enactment - And this too is a court enactment.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 16b:17:2.english: Yirmeya, my son - We read [the text this way].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 16b:17:3.hebrew: שהוחזק - לוה זה כפרן פעם אחרת, לפיכך אין נאמן לומר "פרעתי", ובההיא תנן "יחזיר":
Rashi on Bava Metzia 16b:17:3.english: Where [he] was established - this borrower [was established as] a denier on another occasion; therefore, he is not believed to say, "I have repaid," and regarding that [case] we learned in the Mishnah, "one must return [it]."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 16b:18:1.hebrew: ותו לא פרע כלל - בתמיה. ואי חיישינן לפרעון, זה שלא נזהר לשמור שטרו יפסיד:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 16b:18:1.english: And will he never again repay at all - [This is] a rhetorical question. And if we are concerned about repayment, this [creditor] who was not careful to guard his document should suffer the loss.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 16b:19:1.hebrew: צא תן לו - שפסקו לו דינו בב"ד, שציוו עליו לתת לו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 16b:19:1.english: Go, give [it to] him - That they decided his case in court, [meaning] that they ordered him to give [it] to him.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 16b:1:1.hebrew: משום כדי חייו - מה שתעלה מצודתי היום, תקנו חכמים שיהיו דבריו קיימין, שמא צריך הוא למזונות דבר מועט; אבל מה שתעלה מצודתי כל חדש או כל שנה, אין שם משום כדי חייו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 16b:1:1.english: Because of his livelihood - [Regarding] "what my trap will bring up today," the Sages instituted that his words be valid, for perhaps he needs a small amount for sustenance; but [regarding] "what my trap will bring up all month or all year," there is no [concern] there for his livelihood.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 16b:2:1.english: Acquired by you from now - [Meaning] that when I buy it, I will not be able to retract [from it].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 16b:2:2.hebrew: קנה - אם יקחנה, ואין יכול לחזור כשלקחה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 16b:2:2.english: [The second party] has acquired [it] - If [the first party] buys it, and he cannot retract once he has bought it.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 16b:3:1.hebrew: בשדה סתם - שדה שאני לוקח, ולא אמר "זו", דסמכא דעתיה דמקבל מתנה לסמוך עליו שיקח שדה ויתננה לו, שהרבה שדות מצויות ליקח. אבל אמר לו "שדה זו", לא סמכא דעתיה דמקבל מתנה, ולא האמינו דנימא ניחא ליה דליקו בהימנותיה, ולא מסתבר כוותיה דרב בהא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 16b:3:1.english: With regard to an unspecified field - [Where one said,] "a field that I am buying," and did not say "this [field]," for the gift recipient's mind is confident to rely upon him that he will buy a field and give it to him, since many fields are available to buy. But [if] he said to him, "this field," the gift recipient's mind is not confident, and he does not trust him such that we would say [the giver] wants to uphold his trustworthiness; and it does not stand to reason like Rav in this [case].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 16b:4:1.hebrew: והאלהים - בשבועה. רב אמרה אפילו בשדה זו, דמכדי רב כמאן אמר לשמעתיה? כר"מ כו':
Rashi on Bava Metzia 16b:4:1.english: By God - [This is stated] as an oath: Rav stated it even [in the case of] "this field," for after all, in accordance with whom did Rav state his teaching? In accordance with Rabbi Meir, etc.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 16b:7:1.hebrew: והא אשה כשדה זו דמיא - דיש באלו שאין בידו להביא עצמו לכלל קדושין, כאשר אין ביד זה לכוף את בעל השדה למוכרה לו, דעבד ושפחה אין בידם לשחרר עצמם, ואין ביד אשה להמית את בעלה או אחותה. ואמר רבי מאיר דלכשיבאו לכלל קדושין, מקודשת היא למפרע:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 16b:7:1.english: And isn't [the case of] a woman comparable to "this field" - For there are among these [cases] those where one does not have it in his power to bring himself into a state [capable] of betrothal, just as this [buyer] does not have it in his power to compel the owner of the field to sell it to him: for a slave and a maidservant do not have it in their power to emancipate themselves, and a woman does not have it in her power to put her husband or her sister to death. And [yet] Rabbi Meir says that when they enter a state [capable] of betrothal, she is betrothed retroactively.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 16b:8:1.hebrew: שטר הקנאה - שקנו ממנו שאפילו לא ילוה המעות, שיעבד עצמו לשלמם:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 16b:8:1.english: A deed of transfer - Where they acquired [an obligation] from him that even if he does not borrow the money, he has obligated himself to pay it.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 16b:10:1.hebrew: בשטרי חלטאתא ואדרכתא דלאו בני פרעון נינהו - תימה: שטרי אדרכתא אמאי לאו בני פרעון נינהו, כיון דעדיין לא זכה בקרקע עד שכתבו לו שטרי חלטאתא? וכן בסמוך, דקאמר איהו דאפסיד אנפשיה דבעי ליה למקרעיה או אבעי ליה למכתב שטר מכירה — בשטרי אדרכתא, שעדיין הקרקע היא בידו, במה אפסיד אנפשיה? הלא יכול לטעון "פרעתי"? וי"ל: דשטרי אדרכתא נקט אליבא דרבה, דאית ליה בפרק המפקיד (לקמן בבא מציעא דף לה: ושם) דאכיל פירי מכי מטא אדרכתא לידיה; א"כ, לא יוכל לומר עוד "פרעתי", כיון שכבר זכה בקרקע. ולרבא, דאית ליה מכי שלמו יומי דאכרזתא, לדבריו יעמיד מתני' בחלטאתא גרידא. ויש ספרים דל"ג "אדרכתא":
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 16b:10:1.english: [With regard to] bills of foreclosure and authorization, which are not subject to repayment - This is puzzling: Why are bills of authorization not subject to repayment, since [the creditor] has not yet acquired the land until they write bills of foreclosure for him? And similarly [in the Gemara] immediately following, where [Rava] says that [the debtor] caused the loss to himself, as he should have ripped it up or should have written a bill of sale — with regard to bills of authorization, where the land is still in [the debtor's] possession, how did he cause a loss to himself? Can he not claim, "I have repaid [the debt]"? And one can answer: [The Gemara] mentioned bills of authorization in accordance with Rabbah, who holds in the chapter [entitled] HaMafkid (below, Bava Metzia 35b, and there) that [the creditor] consumes the produce from the time the bill of authorization reaches his hand; if so, [the debtor] can no longer say, "I have repaid," since [the creditor] has already acquired the land. And according to Rava, who holds [that he acquires it only] from the time the days of the public announcement are completed, according to his view he would establish the Mishna [as referring] solely to bills of foreclosure. And there are texts that do not read [the word] "authorization."

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 16b:15:1.hebrew: אע"פ שכתוב בו הנפק לא יחזיר - תימה, דמשמע דאיירי באין חייב מודה, כדאמר שמא כתב ללות ולא לוה, לכך לא יחזיר דחיישינן לפרעון. אבל אם לוה מודה — יחזיר, דלא חיישינן לקנוניא, ולא לשמא פרעו ורוצה לחזור וללות בו כדי להרויח פשיטי דספרא. וקשה, דלקמן (בבא מציעא דף יז.) א"ר יוחנן: שטר שכתוב זמנו בו ביום וכתוב בו הנפק — יחזיר, ומוקי לה רב כהנא כשחייב מודה, ודוקא שכתוב בו ביום, אבל אין כתוב בו ביום — לא יחזיר, או משום פשיטי דספרא או משום קנוניא. וכן לעיל (בבא מציעא דף יג:) אוקי ר"י מתני' דמצא שטרי חוב לא יחזיר בחייב מודה, ומשום קנוניא, דסברי רבנן דאין בו אחריות גבי (לוה) נמי ממשעבדי (ותניא כוותיה דרבי יוחנן). וי"ל דאמוראי נינהו ואליבא דרבי יוחנן: דרב כהנא יעמיד הכא מלתא דרבי יוחנן אף כשחייב מודה, ומשום קנוניא. ורבי אבהו — דמפרש דוקא כשאין חייב מודה, אבל כשחייב מודה יחזיר, דלא חייש לקנוניא — יעמיד נמי מתני' דלעיל כשחייב מודה, ומשום שמא כתב ללות ולא לוה, כרב אסי; אבל היכא דליכא למיחש לכתב ללות ולא לוה, כמו בשטרי הקנאה או כתוב בו הנפק כי הכא — יחזיר, דלא חיישינן לקנוניא. וגמרא דנקט לעיל טעמא דקנוניא — סבר כאביי, דאמר עדיו בחתומיו זכין לו, או אקרי וכתיב לא אמרינן:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 16b:15:1.english: Even if a ratification is written in it, he may not return [it] - This is astonishing, for it implies that [the Gemara] is speaking of [a case] where the debtor does not admit [the debt], as it says, "Perhaps he wrote [it] to borrow and did not borrow"; therefore [where a ratification is written in it], he may not return [it] because we are concerned about repayment. However, if the borrower admits [it], he should return [it], as we are not concerned about collusion [between the borrower and lender to defraud purchasers], nor about [the possibility] that he repaid it and wishes to borrow with it again in order to save the scribe's fees. And this is difficult, for later (Bava Metzia 17a) Rabbi Yoḥanan says: [Regarding] a promissory note whose date is written on that same day, and a ratification is written in it, he should return [it]; and Rav Kahana establishes it [as referring to a case] where the debtor admits [the debt], and specifically where it is written on that same day, whereas if it is not written on that same day, he may not return [it], either because of the scribe's fees or because of collusion. And similarly above (Bava Metzia 13b), Rabbi Yoḥanan established the Mishnah, "[If] one found promissory notes, he may not return [them]," [as referring to a case] where the debtor admits [the debt], and [the reason is] because of collusion, since the Rabbis hold that [even a note that] does not contain a property guarantee collects from encumbered [property] as well (and a baraita was taught in accordance with Rabbi Yoḥanan). And one can say that these are Amoraim [disagreeing] according to Rabbi Yoḥanan: For Rav Kahana would establish Rabbi Yoḥanan's statement here [as applying] even when the debtor admits [the debt], and [the reason is] because of collusion. Whereas Rabbi Abbahu—who explains [Rabbi Yoḥanan's statement here as applying] specifically when the debtor does not admit [the debt], whereas when the debtor admits [it] he should return [it], since he is not concerned about collusion—would also establish the Mishnah above [as applying] when the debtor admits [the debt], and [the reason is] because perhaps he wrote [it] to borrow and did not borrow, like Rav Assi; however, where there is no [reason] to be concerned about "he wrote to borrow and did not borrow," such as with deeds of transfer or [where] a ratification is written in it as here, he should return [it], because we are not concerned about collusion. And the Gemara above, which adopted the reason of collusion, holds like Abaye, who says that its witnesses, through their signatures, acquire [the lien] for him, or [alternatively] we do not say [that] it happened that he wrote [a note without borrowing].

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 16b:18:1.hebrew: ומשום דהוחזק כפרן תו לא פרע כלל - ואף על גב דאמרינן לקמן (בבא מציעא דף יז.) "הוחזק כפרן לאותו ממון", הכא דנפל שאני, דמוכחא מלתא דמשום הכי לא היה נזהר לשומרו, לפי שפרעו הלוה:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 16b:18:1.english: And because he was established as a denier, does he never again repay? - And even though we say later (Bava Metzia 17a) [that] "he is established as a denier with respect to that money," here, where [the document] fell, it is different, because it is evident that for this reason [the creditor] was not careful to guard it — because the borrower [already] paid him.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 16b:2:1.hebrew: שדה שאני לוקח - ל"ג "זו", מדקאמר: "והאלהים, אפילו בשדה זו" — הלא בפירוש אמר "זו":
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 16b:2:1.english: "A field that I am buying" - We do not read [the word] "this" [zo], since [the Gemara later] says: "By God, [Rav said it] even with regard to 'this field'" — [for if "this" were in the text,] did he not explicitly say "this"?

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 16b:2:2.hebrew: קנויה לך מעכשיו - תימה: מה צריך "מעכשיו", כיון דאדם מקנה דבר שלא בא לעולם? דאי לעניין חזרה — הא כל זמן שלא בא לעולם יכול לחזור, אע"ג דאמר "מעכשיו". וי"ל, דנ"מ אם נקרע השטר או שאבד קודם שלקחה זה, דקני כיון דאמר "מעכשיו":
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 16b:2:2.english: "It is acquired by you from now" - This is perplexing: why is "from now" necessary, since [Rav holds that] a person can transfer something that has not yet come into the world? For if [it is needed] with regard to retraction — behold, as long as it has not come into the world, he can retract, even though he said "from now". And one can answer that the practical difference is if the deed was torn or lost before this [seller] purchased it, as [in that case] he [the buyer still] acquires [it] since he said "from now".
